title: cohort-promoter-safety-limiter-and-auto-rollback-policy
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Promotions between LTS/stable channels and nightly/edge builds currently use simplistic percent ramps and manual gating which leads to oscillation, noisy rollbacks, and inconsistent customer experiences when traffic spikes or infra flaps. We need an automated, cohort-aware gatekeeper that enforces promotion budgets, enforces minimum observation windows per cohort, and computes a live safety score to trigger throttles or auto-rollback.

Scope: Design and implement a Cohort Promoter Safety Limiter service and rollout policy that integrates with existing rollout orchestration (traffic-slicer/canary controller), Redwood Console alerting, and runtime telemetry. The service will: compute a health-weighted safety score per promotion cohort, apply dynamic ramp-rate limits, bind percent ramps to LTS channel tiers, and surface human-readable reasons for throttles/rollbacks. It should support feature-flag driven experiments and manual override.

Key capabilities: 
- Cohort model: groups by customer tier, region, route, and API key. Promotions can be targeted at cohorts rather than global percent slices.
- Safety score: combined signal from error-rate delta, latency p95 delta, token-drop-rate, quota-exceeded events, and model-quality regressions (eval hooks). Weighted and configurable per release.
- Ramp limiter: enforces max delta percent/hour per cohort and global concurrency caps to avoid oversubscription of Dedicated pools.
- Auto-rollback policy: conditional rollback if safety score crosses high threshold for sustained window or if sudden spike in critical alert types occurs.
- Graceful degradation: when rollback triggers, automatically shift to a compatible model variant (e.g., quantized fallback or older model version) with circuit-breaker cooldown.
- Observability & explainability: surface the safety score, contributing signals, and decision timeline in Console per-promotion view and in the rollout runbook.
- Integrations: existing rollout API, traffic-slicing controller (ENG-9421), telemetry streams, and alerting rules.

Design trade-offs considered: 
- Strict vs permissive thresholds: conservative defaults to protect SLOs but easy to relax for low-risk experiments.
- Centralized service vs distributed per-region gate: start centralized with region-aware scoring; move to federated if control-plane latency is a bottleneck.
- Automatic rollback vs human-in-the-loop: defaults to auto-rollback for P0 regressions, but allow escalation windows for noisy signals.

Non-goals: full rewrite of rollout orchestration; large UI redesign (only incremental Console panels and runbook links).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Cohort promoter runs in staging and correctly computes safety score from synthetic telemetry for three cohort examples.
2) Ramp limiter enforces configured percent/hour limits and prevents overcommits to Dedicated pools during a simulated spike.
3) Auto-rollback triggers and coordinates a fallback model variant for a staged canary in an integration test.
4) Console shows per-promotion safety score and top-3 contributing signals with links to dashboards.
5) Documentation and runbook in Confluence and an ops playbook for manual overrides are published.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort promoter computes safety score from synthetic and canary telemetry in staging
Ramp limiter enforces percent/hour caps per-cohort and global pool concurrency limits
Auto-rollback flow executes fallback variant and records timeline in audit log
Console surfaces safety score and contributing signals with runbook links
Integration tests covering noisy-signal suppression and cooldown windows
